baslik: One Faulty Update Crashed Millions of Computers at Once
sonuc: crashed millions of Windows computers worldwide
tetik: a faulty configuration file pushed to every machine at once
mekanizma: an out-of-bounds memory read in kernel-level security software causing crashes on boot
ders: the outage pushed staged rollouts and better testing of security updates
zincir: KERNEL DRIVER READS OUT OF BOUNDS
yanilgi: The fix came within hours. Many machines had to be repaired by hand, so outages lingered for days.
tartisma: Security software runs deep inside the system. Should it be allowed that much power?
basliklar: How One CrowdStrike Update Crashed the World
The File That Broke 8.5 Million Computers
soru: How much power should security software have?
sahneler: One morning, millions of Windows computers crashed at the same time.
Suddenly airlines, banks and hospitals around the world went dark.
A security company had pushed out a small configuration file.
Its software ran deep inside the operating system.
The file caused an out-of-bounds memory read.
About eight and a half million machines crashed and couldn't restart properly.
A fix came within hours, but many needed manual repair.
It pushed calls for staged rollouts and better testing.

baslik: A Software Update Killed a Mars Orbiter
sonuc: went silent after nearly a decade at Mars
tetik: a corrective software update containing a memory fault
mekanizma: operators uploading differing parameters, then a correction that wrote to the wrong memory
ders: NASA tightened configuration control for spacecraft software uploads
yanilgi: The spacecraft didn't wear out. A software update caused its loss.
tartisma: The fix for one error created the fatal one. How do you test a patch to a machine millions of miles away?
basliklar: Why NASA Lost Mars Global Surveyor
The Update That Ended a Mars Mission
soru: How do you test a remote patch?
sahneler: After years mapping Mars, NASA's Global Surveyor stopped answering.
Suddenly it went silent, and every attempt to reach it failed.
The orbiter had been working well.
Two operators had updated separate copies of its software with different values.
A corrective update was sent later.
It included a memory fault nobody caught.
That fault caused the loss of the spacecraft.
NASA tightened control of software uploads.

baslik: The Most Expensive Missing Symbol in History
sonuc: veered off course and was destroyed after launch
tetik: a missing overbar in a hand-written guidance equation
mekanizma: unsmoothed velocity data driving erratic steering commands
ders: it underscored thorough software checking before launch
yanilgi: It's often called a missing hyphen. It was actually a missing overbar meaning smoothed data.
tartisma: A tiny notation error became a lost mission. How do you check the math behind code?
basliklar: Why Mariner 1 Was Destroyed
The Missing Symbol That Destroyed a Rocket
sahneler: NASA's first probe to Venus lifted off from Cape Canaveral.
Within minutes it veered off course and was destroyed by range safety.
Its guidance had begun steering erratically.
The problem was in a hand-written equation.
A small bar over one symbol was missing.
That bar meant the data should be smoothed.
Without it, the software reacted to noise.
It became a lesson in checking software before launch.

baslik: The Vienna Bridge That Fell Into the Danube at Dawn
sonuc: collapsed into the Danube early one morning
tetik: a hidden structural failure in the bearings
mekanizma: bearing failure hidden by a massive granite mantle and missed in inspections
ders: Vienna rebuilt the bridge and changed how hidden elements are inspected
yanilgi: Inspectors checked the bridge. The flaw was hidden inside the stone that covered it.
tartisma: Decoration concealed the structure. Should important parts always be visible?
basliklar: Why the Reichsbrücke Collapsed
The Flaw Hidden Inside a Bridge Pier
hook: The flaw was hidden in stone
sahneler: Before dawn, Vienna's Reichsbrücke collapsed into the Danube.
It fell in seconds, and one person was killed.
Traffic was light at that hour.
Its bearings had failed.
The weakness was hidden inside its granite casing.
Inspectors couldn't see it.
An empty city bus fell with it, but the driver survived.
The bridge was rebuilt.

baslik: A Truck Clipped One Beam and a Span Fell
sonuc: lost a span after an oversize load struck it
tetik: an oversize truck load hitting overhead beams
mekanizma: a fracture-critical through-truss with no redundancy once overhead members were hit
ders: oversize load permits and fracture-critical bridges came under review
yanilgi: The bridge wasn't structurally deficient. Its design had no backup if key members were hit.
tartisma: It had been struck by a truck before. Should fracture-critical bridges stay in service?
basliklar: Why the Skagit River Bridge Collapsed
The Truck That Took Down a Span
sahneler: A span of the I-5 bridge over the Skagit River collapsed into the water.
Suddenly two vehicles plunged into the river, but everyone was rescued.
An oversize load had struck the overhead beams.
The truss had no backup if those were damaged.
The span fell immediately.
The bridge had been hit by a truck before.
It wasn't rated structurally deficient.
Oversize load permits and bridge redundancy came under review.

baslik: A Hidden Flaw in an Engine Hub Exploded on Take-off
sonuc: had its engine burst during take-off
tetik: a manufacturing flaw in the engine's fan hub
mekanizma: an uncontained engine failure sending hub debris into the cabin
ders: engine manufacturing and inspection methods were tightened
yanilgi: The engine wasn't worn out. The flaw was created when the part was made.
tartisma: The airline's inspection missed the crack. How do you find flaws inside metal?
basliklar: Why Delta Flight 1288's Engine Exploded
The Flaw Inside an Engine Hub
hook: The engine exploded on the runway
soru: How do you find flaws inside metal?
sahneler: During take-off in Pensacola, an MD-88's left engine burst apart.
Suddenly debris tore into the cabin and killed two passengers.
The pilot aborted the take-off.
Part of the fan hub had fractured.
The flaw had been created during manufacture.
A crack grew from it over time.
The airline's inspection didn't spot it.
Engine inspection methods were tightened.

baslik: The Liner Where the Crew Took the Lifeboats
sonuc: sank after a collision in fog off Newfoundland
tetik: a collision in intermittent fog at full speed
mekanizma: hull damage below the waterline and lifeboats for fewer than half aboard
ders: public outrage fed demands for lifeboats and discipline at sea
yanilgi: The lifeboats weren't used fairly. Most places went to crew and able-bodied men.
tartisma: No women or children survived. What should discipline mean in a sinking?
basliklar: Why the SS Arctic Disaster Was So Deadly
The Sinking Where No Woman Survived
sahneler: In fog off Newfoundland, the liner Arctic collided with a smaller steamer.
It sank hours later, and only eighty eight people survived.
The captain first tried to help the other ship.
Then he found his own hull holed below the waterline.
He ran for land, but the engines stopped.
There were lifeboats for fewer than half aboard.
Order broke down, and crew took many of the places.
All the women and children aboard died.

baslik: The Guard Sent to the Wrong Attic
sonuc: destroyed the cathedral's spire and roof
tetik: a fire in the roof attic
mekanizma: an alarm response sent to the wrong location, delaying the fire brigade
ders: fire detection and response in heritage buildings was re-examined
yanilgi: The alarm worked. The guard was sent to the wrong attic.
tartisma: The alarm didn't call the fire brigade automatically. Should heritage buildings rely on people to confirm?
basliklar: Why Notre-Dame Burned So Badly
The Alarm That Sent a Guard to the Wrong Place
sahneler: Fire broke out in the roof of Notre-Dame de Paris.
Within hours, the wooden spire collapsed through the burning roof.
The fire alarm sounded quickly.
A guard was sent to check, but to the wrong attic.
He found no fire.
The error was discovered about fifteen minutes later.
By then the fire was well advanced.
The alarm system hadn't called the fire brigade automatically.

baslik: The Inaugural Run That Took a Curve at 78 mph
tetik: entering a 30 mph curve at 78 mph
mekanizma: overspeed on a curve without active positive train control and with an inadequately trained engineer
ders: service on the route waited for positive train control
yanilgi: The route was brand new, but the safety system that would have slowed the train wasn't active.
tartisma: The NTSB blamed the transit authority's curve risk and training. Who owns a new route's risks?
basliklar: Why Amtrak 501 Derailed on Its First Run
The Curve Taken at 78 mph
soru: Who owns a new route's risk?
sahneler: On its first run over a new route, an Amtrak train derailed near DuPont, Washington.
Cars fell onto Interstate 5, and three people on board were killed.
The train entered a curve at seventy eight miles per hour.
The limit there was far lower.
Positive train control wasn't active on the track.
The engineer hadn't been adequately trained on the route.
The NTSB faulted the transit authority for the curve's risk.
Service waited for positive train control.

baslik: Two Neglected Dams and a City Swept to the Sea
sonuc: collapsed and flooded the city of Derna
tetik: Storm Daniel's rainfall on unmaintained dams
mekanizma: cascading failure of two embankment dams not maintained for decades
ders: the disaster exposed the cost of neglected dam maintenance
yanilgi: The storm wasn't the only cause. Cracks were reported years earlier, and warnings were ignored.
tartisma: A researcher warned the dams needed urgent attention in 2022. Why are warnings ignored?
basliklar: Why the Derna Dams Collapsed
The Warning Nobody Acted On
sahneler: At night, two dams above Derna, Libya, collapsed one after another.
Suddenly a wall of water swept through the city, killing thousands.
Storm Daniel had dropped enormous rainfall.
The dams hadn't been maintained for years.
Cracks had been reported long before.
A researcher warned they needed urgent attention.
Tens of millions of cubic metres of water rushed downstream.
It became one of the deadliest dam failures in history.
